title: Onboarding Remote Engineers in the First 30 Days
excerpt: A week-by-week plan to turn a new remote hire into a long-term teammate.

author.name: Boyo Martínez
author.bio: Boyo leads product and design at NicaSource, where he helps US companies plan, staff and run nearshore engineering teams. He has spent fifteen years shipping digital products with distributed teams across the Americas.

meta.body:
Introduction

The first thirty days decide whether a remote engineer becomes a long-term teammate or a short-term contractor. A clear plan makes the difference.

Week One: Access and Context

Accounts, repositories and environments should be ready before day one. Pair the new engineer with a buddy and give them a small, real ticket by day three.

Weeks Two and Three: Ownership

A first feature

Assign a scoped feature they can carry from ticket to production, including tests and release notes.

Feedback in both directions

Ask what was confusing. New hires spot gaps in documentation that the rest of the team stopped seeing years ago.

Week Four: Belonging

  • Invite them to present their feature in the team demo.
  • Introduce them to stakeholders outside engineering.
  • Agree on goals for the next quarter in a one-on-one.

Onboarding is the first product your team ships to a new colleague.

Conclusion

A structured first month turns a remote hire into a contributor, and a contributor into someone who stays.
